name: PT MNC Kapital Indonesia Tbk

frontmatter.title: MNC Kapital: a discount to book that the return on equity does not close
frontmatter.summary: BCAP is the listed parent of MNC Bank, an insurer, a multifinance book, a broker and a digital wallet. It trades far below book, but its return on equity sits below its cost of equity, it has never paid a dividend, and its main bank is under OJK attention for a liquidity squeeze. Base value is Rp18; after scenario weighting and the liquidity discount the target is Rp17 against Rp21. REDUCE.
thesis: The low multiple is the discount, not the opportunity: a return on equity of 5.5% in steady state against a cost of equity of 12.2% justifies about 0.18 times book, close to where the shares trade, and residual income, which charges the retained capital, is lower still, although its engine path starts from too high a book and carries a reduced weight [S0].
MNC Bank carries 45.1% of revenue and about seven tenths of group assets, and OJK confirms short-term liquidity pressure with a loan-to-deposit ratio of 105.0% [S3, S10, S11].

No cash reaches shareholders: dividends per share were nil in every year of the pack, the bank has not upstreamed a dividend in the data we hold, and the parent is being pushed to fund its bank [S0, S10, S13].
Insurance, capital markets and digital are growing, so earnings are not the problem; capital, unexplained book-value swings and governance are [S3, S6].

The bear case is far more costly than the bull case is generous because dilution from a rescue is not even in the bear value; the one dated external date we can name is the exchange free-float transition for the bank, 31 March 2027 if the band clause governs and 31 March 2029 if the small-cap clause does, and we have not resolved which [S14].

catalysts.event: Our checkpoint, not an official deadline: has MNC Bank disclosed a concrete capital plan (shareholder injection, strategic investor or consolidation) as pressed by OJK

IDX free-float transition date for listed companies with a float between {{fact.F32|pct}} and {{fact.F31|pct}} (applies to the bank only if the band clause governs; the small-cap clause would give 31 March 2029) and the approximate date of FY2026 audited results (last year's release came on 26 March)
FY2026 RUPST, dividend decision and board slate (last year's meeting was on 25 June)

blocks.text: **Rating REDUCE, target Rp17, price Rp21, expected return -21.2%.** PT MNC Kapital Indonesia is the financial holding of the MNC Group controlled by the Tanoesoedibjo family. Its subsidiaries are a commercial bank (MNC Bank, listed as BABP), general and life insurers, a multifinance and leasing pair, a securities broker and asset manager, and a payments and digital arm [S2, S3]. The shares trade at 0.20 times FY2025 book and 3.5 times FY2025 earnings (price over FY2025 parent earnings per share; the last-twelve-month parent profit in the pack is higher, so the multiple on that basis is a little lower), and the twelve-month range ran from Rp18 to Rp68 [S0]. A screen would call that cheap. We do not.

**Target bridge.** The target is built in three visible steps, so the reader can see how much each overlay contributes. The base scenario alone, valued today, is Rp16 and Rp18 twelve months forward at the cost of equity. Weighting bear, base and bull by 25%, 50% and 25% gives Rp18: with symmetric probabilities and mirrored shocks the weighting costs little, because the bear value (Rp5) is held up by the book-value anchor of the justified multiple while the bull value (Rp32) is geared to the return on equity. The house liquidity table then takes 10% off for a stock that trades about IDR578.8m a day, which gives Rp17. The base-scenario value is itself below the price, so the REDUCE band does not depend on the overlays: the scenario-weighted value (Rp18) is already below the price before the liquidity discount, which is a mechanical rule of the fund (see the valuation section), not our judgement about this name. The rating moved from SELL to REDUCE in this revision because the residual-income leg was re-weighted for a measured bias, explained in the valuation section.

**The variant view.** Cheap-on-book is the base rate for a holding company with a controlling family, no dividend and a subsidiary under regulatory watch; it is not a mispricing by itself. Our model earns the group a return on equity of 5.6% in FY2026E, dips to 5.0% in FY2027E as MNC Bank pays up for deposits, rebounds to 5.8% and settles at 5.5%, one steady-state level of 5.5% that serves both valuation legs. Against a cost of equity of 12.2% that is value-destroying on every retained rupiah, so the justified multiple of book is only 0.18 times. The market is not wrong about the earnings: the reverse calculation says the price needs a FY2027E return on equity of 5.2%, essentially our own path. Where we differ from the price is the retained capital: a group that keeps all earnings at a return below its cost of equity is worth less than the justified multiple, and the residual-income leg (Rp5) prices exactly that, though its engine value is biased low and is weighted at 20% for that reason [S0].

**What the evidence says.** Reported profit is improving: 9M2026 consolidated net profit was IDR182.3bn, up from the prior year on a stable revenue line [S6]. But the nine-month balance sheet already shows the strain: consolidated assets fell to IDR26.86tn from IDR29.04tn at FY2025 year-end, and the pack's cash line fell with it [S6, S13, S0]. Customers then reported a branch withdrawal cap of Rp2m per person in early November, OJK called it a short-term liquidity problem and not a solvency problem, put the bank's loan-to-deposit ratio at 105.0%, and asked the controller to strengthen capital by injection, a strategic investor or a merger [S10, S11]. Core capital at the bank fell to IDR3.03tn from IDR3.27tn a year earlier, though OJK said it remains consistent with the applicable rules [S10]. None of this is in the 30 September accounts, so the fourth quarter is where it will show.
**What moves the value.** First, the return on equity of the bank-heavy earnings stream (see

). Second, the size and form of any recapitalisation: a BCAP rights issue at a depressed price would transfer per-share value to whoever funds it, and that dilution is outside our bear value. Third, any decision to pay a dividend, the first evidence that cash can leave the group. Fourth, an explanation of the large unexplained falls in parent book value, which we could not obtain from the registered sources (the financials section). The probabilities are symmetric (25%, 50% and 25% for bear, base and bull) because the supervisor's own words, the capital adequacy ratio and the float rule give the bull case real support; the skew is in the outcomes, since the bear value excludes dilution.

**Honest limits.** Our evidence is the data pack plus company press releases as reported by the financial press, exchange rules and OJK comments in the press. We have not read the full audited LK or annual report (the company pages were registered but hold only navigation) [S2]. Parent equity moved by large amounts in FY2023 and FY2025 that the sources do not explain, BCAP's own percentage holding in the bank and the holding company's stand-alone debt are not in any registered source, and related-party flows are not quantified. We therefore cannot print a sum-of-the-parts per share and say so in the valuation section. Thin evidence cuts both ways; the rating rests on the return-on-equity gap and retained-capital drag, not on an assumed collapse; a REDUCE, not a SELL, because the one engine leg we know to be biased low no longer carries the full weight.

**Model.** BCAP is a pure holding company: it owns operating subsidiaries and earns through consolidation, not through its own operations [S2, S3]. Reported consolidated revenue in FY2025 was IDR3,770.0bn per the company release, up from IDR3,200.0bn in FY2024, while the data pack's revenue definition gives IDR3,729.7bn [S3, S13, S0]. Net profit including minorities was IDR277.9bn, of which IDR256.0bn belonged to the parent in the pack's cut [S13, S0].

**Segments.** Interest and dividend income, almost all from the bank and the multifinance subsidiaries, is the largest revenue block: IDR1,600.0bn in 9M2026, a little over half of revenue [S6]. Insurance services revenue was IDR806.3bn in FY2025, up on FY2024 at a double-digit rate that the company attributes to credit life and general insurance [S3]; in 9M2026 the same line was IDR923.8bn [S6]. The two shares of revenue the company prints are not comparable: the FY2025 insurance-services line is a smaller share of revenue than the broader insurance-business contribution of 32.0% quoted in the same release, and the 9M2026 share sits on a nine-month revenue base. We therefore claim no growth between the FY2025 and 9M2026 insurance figures, and the model uses neither: revenue comes from the pack's consolidated line. Digital revenue was IDR393.5bn in FY2025 and capital-markets revenue IDR355.8bn, up strongly from small bases [S3]. Multifinance (MNC Finance and MNC Guna Usaha) held IDR2.40tn of assets with a non-performing financing ratio of 1.4%, so it is small and clean [S3].

**MNC Bank is the group.** The bank contributed 45.1% of FY2025 revenue and held IDR20.30tn of the IDR29.04tn of consolidated assets, about seven tenths of the balance sheet, with FY2025 net profit of IDR81.8bn, a capital adequacy ratio of 24.7% and gross NPL of 3.0% [S3, S13]. That bank earned under a third of the group's consolidated profit, so the group's profit is not only bank profit; but the bank is where the capital, the liabilities and the supervisory risk sit [S3].

**Strategy.** Management brands FY2025 as the "digital take-off" of an integrated ecosystem tying bank, payments (MotionPay, FLASH), broker, asset manager and insurer into the MNC Group's media and consumer reach [S3]. The 9M2026 release says the priorities are disciplined growth, digital transformation, partnerships and a capital-strengthening initiative to support expansion; no size or date for that initiative is disclosed [S6].

**Position.** BCAP is a challenger: the bank is a small player by core capital, in the lowest banking group under OJK's capital classification (KBMI tier one) [S10]; the sources give no scale for the insurers or the broker beyond their revenue lines [S3]. The competitive advantage the group claims is an integrated ecosystem of bank, payments, broker and insurer [S3]; the sources give no independent measure of its value.

**Ownership.** Insiders hold 76.7% of the shares and the free float is 36.1%, with 2,125 employees [S0]. The controlling shareholder is Hary Tanoesoedibjo, and the board of commissioners is chaired by Angela Tanoesoedibjo, of the controlling family's name [S5, S13].

Indonesian financial conglomerates built around a bank, an insurer and a broker often use the listed holding as a funding vehicle for the group, and minority holders typically receive little cash from them.

**Industry shape.** BCAP does not fit a single industry. We value it as a financial holding company because the economics are those of a retained-earnings group: its parts are valued off one consolidated return on equity, and the cost of equity is driven by Indonesian rates and country risk, not by a sector beta alone [S0]. The macro deck we use is the house deck: the policy rate 5.8% for FY2027E (spot 5.8%), inflation 3.3%, real GDP growth 5.3%, and an IDR path weakening to 18,350 per US dollar in FY2027E from 18,225 spot [S0]. The firm's macro desk currently tilts away from rate-sensitive Indonesian financials.

**Banking.** The bank's economics depend on deposit costs and the loan-to-deposit ratio. At 105.0%, MNC Bank lends more than it takes in as deposits, so it has to fund the gap with wholesale or interbank money, with capital, or by shrinking loans; the supervisor's own example shows how thin the cushion is, because normal daily withdrawals of about IDR10.0bn could double or triple on social-media-driven panic [S11].

**Insurance, broker and payments.** The insurance arm leans on credit life, which is a by-product of bank and multifinance lending: its growth is, on our reading, tied to the group's own loan origination rather than to independent distribution [S3]. A smaller loan book at the bank therefore trims insurance premium growth too, one reason we model revenue growth of only 3.0% in FY2027E. The capital-markets and digital lines are small, high-growth and lumpy, and compete with far larger broker and e-wallet platforms.

**Regulation.** OJK sets capital tiers, conducts supervision and can require owners to inject capital; LPS insures deposits up to a limit but defers to OJK on individual banks [S10, S12]. The shares' free float is 36.1% [S0].

**Moat and forces.** We see a narrow moat, on the evidence in [S3, S10, S11]. Bargaining power sits with depositors (as the withdrawal episode shows) and with larger banks that set deposit prices; entry barriers in licensed banking and insurance are real but are not a source of excess return for a sub-scale player; substitutes in payments are abundant. The one structural advantage claimed is the integrated group ecosystem, which we cannot quantify from the sources.

**External influences.** Three outside forces matter most. The first is the policy rate path: the house deck holds it flat, so a funding-cost squeeze at the bank would have to come from deposit competition and confidence, not from a rate rise [S0]. The second is the rupiah, which the deck has weakening; BCAP has no stated foreign-currency earnings, so the effect is mostly through investor sentiment and the cost of equity country premium [S0]. The third is supervisory policy, as OJK has signalled that it expects owners to put capital behind their banks and prefers to resolve liquidity problems quietly [S10, S11].

**Group contagion.** In late October the exchange suspended the group's listed media company MSIN for an abnormal cumulative price fall, after it had dropped 75% year to date, and lifted the suspension on 2 November [S7, S8]. That is not a BCAP event, but it shows that investors treat the group's names as one risk.

**History.** Pack revenue grew from IDR2,695.1bn in FY2022 to IDR3,729.7bn in FY2025 [S0]. Parent net profit was IDR136.4bn, IDR55.9bn, IDR87.1bn and IDR256.0bn over FY2022 to FY2025, so FY2025 is the best year and the first with a return on equity above four percent (4.4%) [S0]. FY2025 earnings per share were 6.0 on 42,619 million shares, unchanged in every year, so there has been no dilution to date [S0].

**9M2026.** Consolidated profit of IDR182.3bn was higher than a year earlier, with revenue described as relatively stable; total equity including minorities was IDR5.36tn against IDR5.42tn at FY2025 year-end, so book fell slightly despite the profit [S6, S13]. Our FY2026E assumes the fourth quarter lands between the nine-month run-rate and the unusually strong Q4 2025, giving parent profit of IDR256.8bn and a return on opening equity of 5.6%, above FY2025's 4.4% on the evidence of higher nine-month profit [S6, S0].

**The book-value question.** Parent equity fell from IDR5,775.2bn at FY2024 to IDR4,585.6bn at FY2025 although parent profit was IDR256.0bn, a fall of more than four times that year's profit, and it fell again over 9M2026 against a profit of IDR182.3bn (consolidated equity including minorities went from IDR5.42tn to IDR5.36tn) [S0, S6, S13]. Parent equity had also jumped between FY2022 (IDR5,353.6bn) and FY2023 (IDR6,155.5bn) on a profit of only IDR55.9bn [S0]. We searched the registered company and press sources for the cause and found none: the company's investor pages hold only navigation, and the press releases give totals and no equity bridge [S2, S3, S6, S13]. The candidates are fair-value moves on the bank's and insurers' securities, a change in insurance accounting, a change in group structure that moved equity to minorities, or a distribution; we cannot tell which, and a related-party transfer would be a different order of problem from a mark-to-market. Consolidated equity tells the same story more strongly. Total equity including minorities was IDR5.42tn at FY2025. At FY2024 the same company release gives assets of IDR29.40tn and liabilities of IDR22.30tn [S3, S13], so consolidated equity at FY2024 was far above the FY2025 figure: the consolidated fall is several times the whole of FY2025 consolidated profit of IDR277.9bn, and larger than the parent's own fall, so the minorities' share dropped as well. Assets were flat while liabilities rose, which fits a remeasurement or reclassification better than cash leaving: the pack's consolidated cash rose over FY2025 and its debt fell [S0]. On the EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS test we therefore classify the movement as optics-class, provisionally: aggressive or opaque but with no sign yet of fabricated cash or value moving to an affiliate, which is what would make it manipulation-class. The note that would resolve it is the statement of changes in equity and the note on the first application of the new insurance-contract standard (PSAK 74) and on non-controlling interests in the FY2025 audited LK, which we have not been able to read [S2]. We treat it as an unresolved optics-class flag and do three things. The valuation uses the 30 September 2026 parent book value as its opening equity, not the model's year-end path. The bear case in the risks section names a further leak of the same kind as a tail beyond the modelled value. And the governance section carries it as a flag that would turn manipulation-class if the LK shows value moving to a related party.

Indonesian groups that own insurers and hold government and corporate bonds can see book value move sharply when bond prices or insurance accounting standards change, without any cash leaving the group.

**Why the model's equity path sits above the 30 September balance.** The engine rolls equity from the FY2025 close by adding each year's profit and subtracting dividends; it has no line for other equity movements. Its FY2026E year-end equity is IDR4,842.4bn, against the 30 September parent book (the opening equity of the residual-income leg), a gap larger than the fourth-quarter profit could close, because the nine-month movement was negative despite profit and the template cannot carry that. We could not re-base the path inside the engine, so we measured the effect instead of leaving it open. We re-ran the residual-income leg outside the engine with the modelled path lowered by the full gap, once with profit held at the model's level and once with profit following the return on equity on the lower book (the consistent treatment, since the return is stated on opening equity). The leg rises from its engine value of Rp5 to between two and three times that, and the full-weight blend with justified price-to-book then gives a target in the REDUCE band, not the SELL band (the working is in the assumptions file, under the weights justification). The justified price-to-book leg uses the actual 30 September book and is unaffected. Because the engine cannot rebase, we set the residual-income weight at the level at which the engine's biased leg reproduces that rebased blend, which is 20% against 80% on the primary. Dropping the leg altogether would put the target within the HOLD band, so the choice of weight matters, and we show both ends here rather than hide it. The return-on-equity path itself is stated on opening parent equity and is the figure the market and management would recognise [S0, S6].

**Forecasts.** Revenue grows 2.0% in FY2026E and 3.0% in FY2027E (the bank must shrink lending to cut its loan-to-deposit ratio), then 5.0% to 5.5% as insurance, markets and digital take more of the mix [S0, S6, S11]. Return on equity is 5.0% in FY2027E for a higher deposit cost and credit cost at the bank, then 5.8% as the deferred earnings return, and 5.5% and 5.5% from FY2029E. We removed an earlier ramp to a higher return: with revenue growing about as fast as nominal GDP and no margin assumption, a rising return would mean unsourced margin expansion; the segment growth in capital markets, digital and insurance is carried by the bull case. Minorities take 7.0% of profit, payout is 0.0% through FY2030E and the share count is flat, because the capital plan is undisclosed [S0, S6, S13]. From FY2031E a long-run payout is needed for the terminal growth rate to be consistent with the return on equity (retain only what growth requires), which is why dividends appear late in the horizon. Parent equity grows from IDR4,585.6bn to IDR5,084.5bn by FY2027E and IDR5,987.4bn by FY2030E; book value per share goes from 107.6 to 140.5. Earnings per share rise to 7.3 by FY2030E.

**Cash flow and the balance sheet.** The pack's LTM operating cash flow is deeply negative and cash fell between year-end and September, matching the reduction in consolidated assets; for a group that consolidates a bank, operating cash flow mostly reflects deposits and loans, not earnings quality, so we do not read an accruals ratio from it [S0, S6]. Capital expenditure is small against the profit line. The group's own capital is not the issue today (the bank's capital adequacy ratio was 24.7% at FY2025) but its liquidity, and the cushion fell with core capital [S3, S10].

**Earnings-quality screen.** First, accruals: not meaningful for a bank-bearing balance sheet; we use provisioning and asset-quality trends instead, and gross NPL improved to 3.0% at the bank and multifinance NPF was 1.4% in FY2025 [S3]. Second, divergence: no receivable or inventory build to test; the fall in consolidated assets while profit rose is the divergence that matters. Third, unexplained equity movements, described above: an optics-class flag we cannot close, and we rely on the latest balance sheet rather than an average [S0]. Fourth, IDX regime: BCAP is not on the special-monitoring or concentration lists we could verify, and had no suspension of its own [S7, S8]. Fifth, related-party share of revenue: not disclosed in anything we could read; thin evidence. Sixth, structure flags: no rights issue to date, pledged-share status unknown, auditor not sourced; none found, but not all checked. Nothing manipulation-class was found.

**Calibration.** Our FY2026E return on equity is above the last actual by about one point, justified by the nine-month profit growth; every later year is held at or near that level, not above it [S6].

**Why this method set.** A holding company that owns a bank, insurers and a broker, pays no dividend and is valued by the market against book is best framed by what each retained rupiah earns relative to the cost of equity. We therefore use justified price-to-book as the primary method (80% weight) and residual income as the cross-check (20%). The house default also includes a P/E and a dividend-discount leg; we drop both. The P/E leg used the pack's own five-year average multiple, which rests on years of crisis-depressed profit and returned a value many times the price; the DDM is zero by construction because no dividend has ever been paid [S0, S13].

**Cost of equity.** The risk-free rate is 7.4%, the mature-market equity risk premium 4.2%, the Indonesia country premium 2.5% and the beta 0.95 (unlevered 0.95, no financial leverage at holdco level), giving a cost of equity of 12.2% [S0].

Terminal growth is 4.0%, deliberately below nominal GDP. The house macro deck has real GDP growth of 5.3% and inflation of 3.3%, which compound to a nominal rate roughly twice our terminal rate. We hold the terminal rate down because the group's steady-state return on equity sits far below its cost of equity: a capital base that earns less than it costs cannot be assumed to grow at the pace of the economy, since retained earnings fund book growth only at the return on equity times the retention rate. The return-on-equity path, not terminal growth, carries the view [S0].

**One steady-state return on equity.** Both legs now use the same long-run return of 5.5%: the justified multiple is the average of the first three forecast years' return, and the residual-income leg runs the explicit path to its terminal value at 5.5%, the two within a few hundredths of a point. A previous draft used a lower sustainable return in the multiple than in the residual-income path; the challenge that this was an unsourced inconsistency was right, and we resolved it by holding the path flat rather than by raising the multiple, because only the flat path is consistent with revenue growth and no margin expansion. Had the return recovered to the earlier higher level in both legs, the justified multiple would be well above today's and the target would be near the price; that outcome is carried by the bull case (Rp32), where the return is one point higher.

**Result.** Justified price-to-book is 0.18 times on that return, a value of Rp19 a share. Residual income gives Rp5, which is -75.4% against the primary. The divergence has a specific cause: the justified multiple assumes earnings are distributed in the proportion that lets book value grow at the terminal rate, while the explicit residual-income path keeps all earnings in the group for five years at a return below the cost of equity, which destroys value each year the capital stays. We do not change the terminal treatment: the residual is grown at the terminal rate from a book value that, from FY2031E, grows at that same rate because the long-run payout is set to make it so; fading the residual to zero would give the retained capital a free pass that the long-run payout assumption already denies. The two legs are therefore a statement about dividend policy, and the blend leans on the primary. As noted in the financials section, the overstated modelled book biases the residual-income leg downward, which is why that leg carries 20% of the blend and not the larger weight we first gave it; the divergence figure above is the biased engine value, not the rebased one. Sizing the bias: about seven percent of modelled equity, roughly three hundred billion rupiah of excess, lifts the residual-income value by about three rupiah a share and the blend, at that leg's weight, by under one rupiah, which leaves the target and the REDUCE rating unchanged because the base-scenario value stays below the price after the adjustment. The blend is Rp16 today and Rp18 a year forward in the base scenario; after probability weighting across scenarios (Rp18) and the 10% liquidity discount, the target is Rp17 [S0].

**The liquidity discount.** The discount is not our estimate. It is the fund's house liquidity table, applied by the engine to any name whose average daily traded value (about IDR578.8m here) falls below the table's bands, and the analyst cannot waive it for a single name. We acknowledge the argument that a low price already reflects thin trading; the table exists precisely because the fund cannot exit such a position at the screen price, and the REDUCE band holds before it is applied, because the base-scenario value is below the price without it [S0].
**Sensitivity.** The value is highly geared to the return on equity because it is a multiple of the gap to the cost of equity.

**Sum of the parts, and why we cannot print one.** The holdco card asks for each listed stake at market or house value, unlisted parts at book or a multiple, less holding-company debt. We tried and report where it breaks. BCAP's percentage holding in the bank is not in any registered source, and nor is the parent-only net debt, so a per-share sum would need two invented inputs; the template for financial equities also has no sum-of-the-parts method. What we can say with sourced figures is bounded. At 0.20 times FY2025 book the shares already trade at a discount to a book-marked sum of the parts of about four fifths, far wider than the discount in any year-end of the pack's four-year history, whose lowest multiple (FY2023) was still above today's [S0]. But the bank is about seven tenths of the assets, and our own coverage of the bank itself is a SELL with a target far below its price: the bank's shares have fallen 65.5% this year to a price near the low of their range [S15]. Marking the bank at its house value, or even at its market value, takes most of it out of a book-marked sum of the parts, so a market- or house-marked sum is below a book-marked one, not above it. That is consistent with our target for the holding company being far below book, and it reconciles the two ratings: a holding company whose main asset our own work values at a fraction of book cannot be a buy on the price-to-book discount. Upstream dividends are nil: the holding company pays nothing and the data we hold show no dividend from the bank, so upstream coverage of any holdco dividend is zero and the stock has no cash yield to anchor a narrowing of the discount. The holdco archetype (a discount narrowing to its own range) needs a dated catalyst; the only dated one we can name is in the final section [S14].

**What the price implies.** The price implies a FY2027E return on equity of 5.2%, close to our 5.0%. The market therefore agrees with our earnings; what it will not do is pay more than the justified multiple of book for them, and we think it is right not to. A re-rating toward the shares' own historical multiple of book would need the return on equity to rise toward the cost of equity, a recapitalisation without dilution, or a first dividend: we model none of these in the base case [S0].

**Divergences.** The wide divergence is between justified price-to-book and residual income, explained above. A multiple-based P/E value would be several times the price on trailing profit, but we do not accept it, as the multiple it uses came from years when profit was one-third to one-tenth of today's.

**Liquidity and capital at MNC Bank (likelihood high, impact high).** OJK has acknowledged short-term liquidity pressure at a bank with a loan-to-deposit ratio of 105.0% and falling core capital, and has asked the owner for a capital plan [S10, S11]. LPS declined to comment and defers to OJK [S12]. A recapitalisation by BCAP shareholders would be dilutive; if BCAP funds it from its own cash or by selling insurance or multifinance assets, the earnings base shrinks.

**Dilution (medium, high).** Management itself refers to a capital-strengthening initiative [S6]. Share count is unchanged in our base case because nothing is sized; a rights issue at a depressed price would cut value per share. The engine's financial template holds the share count at the balance-sheet date for valuation and has no injection line, so this dilution is not in the scenario values below: it is an additional tail, and the reader should treat the bear value as a floor on earnings, not on the shares.

**Book-value leak (medium, high).** The unexplained falls in parent equity (the financials section) could recur if the cause is structural. A further fall on the scale of FY2025 would remove a large part of the equity the justified multiple is applied to, and it is not in the bear value either.

**Governance and group contagion (medium, medium).** Related-party exposure is not quantified; a board director appointed at the June 2026 meeting resigned on 6 November and was replaced by a group executive [S13, S5]. The sister company MSIN was suspended and then released [S7, S8], and the parent of the media group faces a first-instance damages award of IDR484.0bn in an unrelated commercial case that is under appeal [S15].
**Macro and rates (medium, medium).** A higher policy rate lifts deposit cost; the house macro deck holds the rate at 5.8% [S0]. The firm's macro desk tilt on rate-sensitive financials is to avoid.
**Liquidity of the stock (high, low to medium).** Trading value is thin [S0]; the house liquidity discount of 10% applies.
**Scenarios.**

Each scenario's value as a multiple of book can be read against the pack's own history: even the bull value of Rp32 is roughly a quarter of the current book value per share and so still below the lowest year-end multiple of book in the four years of history (FY2023); the base value of Rp18 is about a seventh of book; and the bear value of Rp5 is a few percent of book [S0].

**Bear (25%, Rp5).** The deposit run is not contained and the group's return on equity stays near the FY2025 level of 4.4%, with revenue growth two points lower in every year [S10, S11]. The engine carries those two shocks and nothing else. The larger damage described in the risk list, a discounted BCAP rights issue, the sale or pledge of the insurance and multifinance arms, a mark-down of the bank and a further book-value leak, is outside the value; our house view on the bank is a SELL with a target far below its price, and a bank marked there would leave BCAP with little more than its non-bank parts. We say this plainly because the engine's bear value cannot show the extra loss.
**Base (50%, Rp18).** The episode is managed with a capital plan that does not hit minority holders, earnings drift as described in the financials section, and no dividend is paid through FY2030E.

**Bull (25%, Rp32).** The supervisor's description is right. OJK called the problem technical and short-term, said that core capital remains consistent with the rules, and called the loan-to-deposit ratio something that normally moves up and down [S10, S11]; the bank's capital adequacy ratio was 24.7% at FY2025 [S3]. The bank's free float sits below the exchange's new minimum of 15.0%, so a placement of new bank shares to the public or to a strategic investor is a natural recapitalisation route that does not need BCAP's own cash [S14]. Capital-markets and digital revenue reached IDR355.8bn and IDR393.5bn in FY2025 on strong growth rates, and the insurance line grew at a double-digit rate [S3]. The return on equity is one point above the base and revenue growth two points above, the mirror of the bear shocks. The probabilities are symmetric: the live supervisory case at the largest subsidiary is offset by the supervisor's reassuring words and the float rule.

**Signposts that would change the view.** Upgrade: a sized, non-dilutive recapitalisation; a first dividend; the loan-to-deposit ratio below the regulatory comfort level; core capital rebuilding; an explanation of the equity falls that shows no value left the group. Downgrade: a BCAP rights issue, a withdrawal cap that persists, OJK enforcement against the bank, a further unexplained fall in book value, further group suspensions.

**Ownership and control.** Insiders hold 76.7% and the free float is 36.1% [S0]. The controller is Hary Tanoesoedibjo, and the board of commissioners is chaired by Angela Tanoesoedibjo [S5, S13, S10]. The firm's konglo registry does not classify BCAP as a konglo-group member and it is not on the concentrated-ownership list we checked; this is a disclosure status and not a finding of wrongdoing.

**Related parties and pledges.** The group's bank, payments, insurance and finance arms share a brand and a controller [S2, S3]. We could not quantify related-party revenue, loans to affiliates or pledged shares from the sources; we flag that as thin evidence, not as a clean result. Combined with the unexplained falls in parent equity described in the financials section, this is a governance flag: until the LK shows where the equity went, we cannot rule out value moving to affiliates, and we would treat a confirmed transfer as manipulation-class.
**Auditor and opinion.** Not sourced. The annual accounts were approved at the June 2026 meeting without a dividend [S13].

**Dividends.** Dividends per share were 0.0 in every year of the pack [S0, S13]. A group that has not paid for four years while its bank is being asked for fresh capital is not going to start before the bank is fixed.

**Board.** The June 2026 meeting reappointed all commissioners and added two directors; one resigned on 6 November and was replaced by a group executive with long service [S13, S5]. Short tenure of an appointed director during an OJK supervisory episode is a governance signal, though not a finding.

**ESG.** The main exposures are customer protection and conduct at the bank (the withdrawal complaints), data and cyber risk in a payments business, and concentrated-ownership governance. The 2025 sustainability report was approved at the meeting but we did not read it [S13].

**Dated catalysts.** First, 31 March 2027: the exchange's transition date for listed companies whose free float sits between 12.5% and 15.0%, which on the bank coverage file's float figure includes MNC Bank. That date applies only if the band clause governs. The same article gives companies with a market value below IDR5.00tn until 31 March 2029, and MNC Bank's market value on the bank coverage file is a fraction of that threshold, so the small-cap clause may govern and the date would then be 2029 [S14]. We have not resolved which clause governs, so we do not call 31 March 2027 enforceable: it is a possible, not a certain, external prompt. A bank-level placement would meet either date and double as a recapitalisation, which is why it is the best-defined external discount catalyst we can name, but it is conditional on the clause. Second, FY2026 audited accounts around the end of March 2027: last year's release came on 26 March [S3]. Third, the June 2027 shareholders' meeting and its dividend decision (last year's was on 25 June) [S13]. Our own checkpoint of 31 December 2026 for a concrete capital plan is not a deadline: OJK has named no date in the sources [S10, S11].

**Upstream dividend coverage.** The holding company's coverage of its own dividend by cash received from subsidiaries is zero: no dividend is paid to BCAP shareholders, and the data we hold show none from the bank [S0, S13]. The implication under the holdco method is the widest warranted discount in the range, and a first upstream dividend is the cleanest evidence we would accept that the discount can narrow.

**What we would do on each outcome.** If a sized and non-dilutive capital plan appears, we would re-run the model with the injection in the valuation bridge and likely move the rating up, since the main discount driver would have been addressed. If a BCAP-level rights issue is announced, we would model the dilution and the issue price explicitly before the next update. If the fourth-quarter accounts show deposits and assets still falling, we would lower the forecast return on equity and revisit the bear probability [S6, S10].

**KPIs between updates.** We watch these every quarter and on any OJK or exchange announcement. MNC Bank loan-to-deposit ratio and core capital (currently 105.0% and IDR3.03tn), withdrawal limits at the branch, consolidated assets against IDR26.86tn at 9M2026, parent return on equity against 5.6%, the parent equity bridge in the next LK, insurance revenue growth against IDR923.8bn in 9M2026, any related-party disclosure and any rights-issue or dividend announcement [S6, S10, S11].

bear.narrative: MNC Bank's deposit outflow is not contained: deposit cost jumps, credit cost rises on the SME and consumer book and the group's return on equity stays near the FY2025 actual of about 4.4%, with revenue growth two points below the base. The engine carries this as a one-point lower return on equity and two points lower revenue growth in every year. A discounted BCAP rights issue or a mark-down of the bank to its house value would cost more than this: the template holds the share count at the balance-sheet date and has no injection line, so that dilution tail is described in the risk section, not valued here.

bull.narrative: The MNC Bank episode is resolved as the supervisor described it - a short-liquidity problem, with core capital "masih sesuai dengan ketentuan" (S10) and LDR that "biasa naik turun" (S11), starting from a 24.7% capital adequacy ratio (S3) - and a strategic investor, a group injection or the bank's own free-float placement (the bank's float sits below the 15% IDX minimum, S14) recapitalises it without material BCAP dilution. Insurance, capital markets (+69.1% in FY2025) and digital (+28.8%) keep compounding (S3), so return on equity runs one point above the base and revenue growth two points above, the mirror of the bear shocks.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs ROE and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: LTM revenue Rp3,723.5bn against FY2025A Rp3,729.7bn is flat (S0), and management describes 9M2026 as "kondisi pendapatan yang relatif stabil" (S6). FY2026E held at 2% real-terms-neutral; FY2027E 3% because the bank must shrink its loan book to cut a 105% LDR (S11) and pay up for deposits; 5-5.5% from FY2028E as insurance, capital markets and digital keep taking share of the mix.

assumptions.label: ROE on opening equity
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the last actuals and held flat, not ramped. FY2025 consolidated net profit was Rp277.9bn (S13) with parent profit Rp256.1bn (S0), a 4.4% return on opening parent equity. 9M2026 consolidated profit is Rp182.3bn, +18.6% yoy (S6), so FY2026E assumes Q4 lands between the 9M quarterly run-rate and the unusually strong Q4 2025 (FY2025 less 9M2025 is about Rp124bn): about Rp255bn to parent, 5.6% of FY2025 closing parent equity Rp4,585.6bn (S0). FY2027E is cut to 5.0% for the MNC Bank funding shock - OJK confirms "tekanan likuiditas jangka pendek" (S11), core capital fell to Rp3.03trn from Rp3.27trn (S10) and customers report a Rp2m branch withdrawal cap (S10) - which lifts deposit cost and credit cost at the subsidiary that holds roughly seven tenths of group assets (S3). FY2028E rebounds to 5.8% as the deferred earnings return, then settles at 5.5% from FY2029E. One steady-state ROE of 5.5% therefore serves both valuation legs (the engine's sustainable ROE is the mean of FY2026E-28E, 5.47%, against the 5.5% terminal path used by the residual-income leg). The earlier ramp to 6.6% by FY2030E is dropped: with revenue growth of 5% and no margin assumption it implied net profit growth of about 10% a year, an unsourced margin expansion; the recovery of the insurance (+15.0%), capital-markets (+69.1%) and digital (+28.8%) lines in FY2025 (S3) is carried by the bull case (+1pp), not by the base. Nothing is assumed above what 9M2026 supports.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: LTM minorities are 5.9% of consolidated net profit ((306.5-288.3)/306.5, S0) and FY2025 was 7.9% (21.9/277.9, S0/S13); the 21.2% three-year average is distorted by FY2024 when group profit was unusually small. Held at 7% across the horizon, in line with the last two actual years.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: No dividend in any year of the pack's history (dps 0.0 FY2022A-FY2025A, S0) and the FY2025 RUPST approved the accounts and the director changes without declaring one (S13). Base case retains all earnings: OJK is pushing shareholder capital into MNC Bank (S10) and management itself flags a "rencana inisiatif penguatan modal" (S6). Payout therefore stays at zero - the honest read of a holdco that has never upstreamed cash to its own shareholders. From FY2031E the long-run payout is 27%: with terminal growth of 4% (see terminal_growth) and a steady-state ROE of 5.5%, book value can only grow at 4% if 1 - 4%/5.5% of earnings is distributed - the same identity the justified P/BV leg uses - so a perpetuity that retained everything would contradict its own growth rate. The five explicit years stay at zero because the capital plan is unresolved (S10, S6).

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Share count is 42,618.85m in every year of the pack (S0). A BCAP-level rights issue is a live risk (S6 capital-strengthening initiative) but no size or date is disclosed, so it is carried in the bear case and in the dilution risk section rather than in the base case.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for an IDR reporter: 4.0%, deliberately below nominal GDP. The macro deck's FY2027E real GDP is 5.29% and CPI 3.28% (house deck), which compounds to a nominal growth rate near 8.6%; 4.0% is therefore about half of nominal GDP, not in line with it. The cap is the economics of this group: a financial holding whose steady-state return on equity (5.5%) sits far below its cost of equity cannot grow its equity base at the economy's pace without destroying value, and retained earnings alone fund book growth at about the return on equity times the retention rate, so a terminal rate near the long-run house inflation rate (the deck's CPI) plus a little real growth is the most the capital base can carry. The ROE path, not terminal growth, carries the view.

challenges.challenge: Justified P/BV uses roe_sustainable 0.054667, which equals the mean of FY2026E-28E ROE (5.6%, 5.0%, 5.8%), while the model's own ROE is 6.6% from FY2030E to FY2035E and the RI leg uses that path. At 6.6% the justified multiple is (0.066-0.04)/(0.1219-0.04) = 0.32x against 0.18x, i.e. about Rp34 against Rp19 on BVPS 106.05. A 1.1pp unsourced difference between two legs of the same model more than halves the primary value and flips the rating (blend about Rp25, target near the price).
challenges.answer: Inconsistency was real. One steady-state ROE of 5.5% now serves both legs: path held flat (5.6/5.0/5.8/5.5/5.5, lt 5.5), engine mean of FY2026E-28E is 5.47%. The unsourced ramp to 6.6% is dropped (5% revenue growth with no margin change cannot give ~10% profit growth) and sits in the bull case. Rating moves to SELL at the new target; the 6.6% outcome is shown by the bull value. [S0, S3, S6]

challenges.challenge: The report says a SOTP cannot be run because the bank's market value is not in the pack. BABP.JK is a covered name (datapack price Rp24, mcap Rp1,067bn, free float 12.76%, house target Rp2.2 in its own report). The holdco card requires listed stakes at market or house value, the current discount to SOTP vs its own history, and upstream dividends. BCAP at 0.2x book with the bank about 70% of assets is exactly the case.
challenges.answer: Added a SOTP discussion in section 4: the financial_equity template has no SOTP method, BCAP's stake in BABP and parent-only debt are in no registered source, so no per-share SOTP is printed. Gives the P/B discount vs own history, the bank at market/house value (BABP SELL, shares down 65% YTD [S15]) lowering a book-marked SOTP, zero upstream dividend, and the reconciliation to the SELL. [S14, S15]

challenges.challenge: Parent equity fell from Rp5,775bn to Rp4,586bn in FY2025 (-Rp1,189bn) on Rp256bn profit, and the 9M2026 balance sheet shows Rp4,520bn despite about Rp170bn parent profit. Report admits it is unexplained. Book value is the base of the justified P/BV and the cash/asset shrinkage (assets 29.04 to 26.86tn) is not in the bear case.
challenges.answer: Searched the registered company and press sources: no equity bridge exists in any (IR pages hold navigation only, S2). Cause stays unexplained; added FY2024-25 parent equity fall (>4x profit) and 9M2026 equity-vs-profit to section 3, an optics-class flag with a manipulation-class trigger, a book-value-leak risk and a governance flag. Valuation opening equity is the 9M2026 balance. [S2, S6, S13]

challenges.challenge: Bear narrative describes a deeply discounted rights issue and sale or pledge of insurance and multifinance, but the bear model shocks only ROE -1pp and revenue growth -2pp with share_change 0 and no write-down of the bank. The house sibling view on BABP is SELL Rp2.2 (-90%). Bear Rp6 is therefore a mild earnings shock, not the described rescue.
challenges.answer: Rewrote the bear narrative to match its two shocks (ROE -1pp, growth -2pp). The engine fixes shares at the balance-sheet date (market() shares_m) and has no injection or write-down line, so dilution and a bank mark-down cannot be valued; the risk section and bear paragraph state they are an extra tail beyond the bear value, with the BABP SELL as context. With the ROE now flowing into both legs the bear is Rp4, already near zero. [S10, S11, S15]

challenges.challenge: Model equity path starts from FY2025A 4,586 and gives FY2026E 4,842 (+257), while the 9M2026 balance sheet shows 4,520 (valuation uses 4,520). Reaching 4,842 needs about Rp322bn of Q4 equity gain against a Q4 parent profit of about Rp70-95bn. ROE and forward BV path in FY2027E+ are therefore on an overstated denominator, inconsistent with valuation opening equity.
challenges.answer: Engine equity rolls forward as prior equity + profit - dividends with no other-equity line, so the path cannot be re-based inside the engine (not editable). Section 3 now bridges FY2026E model equity to the 9M2026 balance sheet, uses 9M2026 book as valuation opening equity (P/BV leg unaffected), and states the effect: the overstated denominator lowers the residual-income leg, so the cross-check is biased down, not up. ROE path stated on opening equity. [S0, S6]

challenges.challenge: A 10% liquidity discount is deducted from a stock already priced at 0.2x book and described by the report as carrying a governance and capital discount; ADTV Rp579m is already reflected in the price. It is the difference between a base-only decline of about 10% and the -22% headline. Also RI applies 4% terminal growth to a perpetually negative residual (pv_tv -1,951), which compounds the shortfall and drives the -31% RI divergence.
challenges.answer: The 10% is not an analyst discount: it is constitution fund record coverage.liquidity_discount (ADTV below Rp2bn), applied by cov_engine to every thin name and not waivable per name; ADTV is Rp0.58bn [S0]. The SELL holds before it (base value below price). RI terminal growth: after the ROE fix the residual grows at g from a book that also grows at g (payout 27% from FY2031E), the same identity as the P/BV leg, so fading it to zero would give retained capital a free pass; the gap is the five zero-payout years at ROE below COE. Both explained in section 4. [S0]

challenges.challenge: Bull omits sourced positives: OJK said core capital 'masih sesuai dengan ketentuan' (S10), called LDR 'biasa naik turun' (S11), CAR was 24.7% (F16), BABP free float 12.76% is below the 15% IDX minimum so a bank-level placement is a natural recapitalisation path, and FY2025 capital-markets (+69%) and digital (+28.8%) growth. Bull Rp32 equals only about 0.30x book, still below the lowest historical P/BV in the pack (0.35x in FY2023).
challenges.answer: Bull now cites OJK on core capital and LDR [S10, S11], CAR 24.7% [S3], the bank's float below the 15% IDX minimum as a placement route [S14] and FY2025 capital-markets/digital/insurance growth [S3]. Scenario probabilities made symmetric (25/50/25). Implied P/BV added: bull about a quarter of book, base a seventh, bear a few percent, all below the lowest history multiple (FY2023). [S0, S3, S10, S11, S14]

challenges.challenge: Holdco card requires a named and dated discount catalyst and upstream-dividend coverage. Catalysts listed are undated ('before year-end, not committed'), FY2026 accounts (late March) and the June 2027 AGM; BABP has never upstreamed a dividend and none is analysed. A BABP free-float deadline (from March 2027) is not used.
challenges.answer: Dated catalyst added: 31 March 2027 IDX free-float deadline for companies with 12.5-15% float (bank in band per its coverage file; below Rp5tn mcap otherwise 2029) [S14]; checkpoint 31 Dec 2026 labelled as ours (OJK named no deadline). Upstream dividend coverage stated as zero with its implication; catalysts frontmatter updated. [S10, S11, S14]

challenges.challenge: Insurance revenue is quoted on two definitions: F27 Rp806.3bn = 21.4% of FY2025 revenue (S3) and F26 32.0% in the same source; 9M2026 Rp923.8bn = 31.7% (F12). Text says 'growing at a double-digit rate ... close to a third of revenue', mixing a 21.4% base year with a 31.7% current share, which implies 9M annualised growth of about 50% that the report never claims.
challenges.answer: Insurance revenue restated per definition: FY2025 services line (F27) vs broader insurance-business share (F26) vs 9M2026 on a nine-month base (F12); no growth claimed across them and the model uses neither (revenue from the pack's consolidated line). [S3, S6]

challenges.challenge: The summary says the market 'prices the earnings correctly' and base value is close to the price, yet the REDUCE call at -22% is built on probability-weighting plus a discount. Text should state that base-scenario value alone is Rp18.6 (-11%) and how much of the gap each overlay contributes.
challenges.answer: Summary now has a target bridge: base-scenario value, scenario-weighted value, then the mechanical liquidity discount to the target; base alone is below the price so the SELL does not rest on the overlays. Rating is SELL after C1. [S0]

challenges.challenge: QC Q7 unanswered, and s7 still calls the 31 March 2027 free-float deadline 'the one external, dated and enforceable' catalyst although the same S14 article gives issuers under Rp5tn market cap (BABP mcap about Rp1.07tn) until 31 March 2029. Which clause governs is unresolved. The report lists both dates but keeps the enforceable claim and the s0 line that the March 2027 deadline is the dated hard point.
challenges.answer: Dropped 'enforceable' and the hard-point wording in s0 and s7; both S14 dates stated, 31 March 2027 only if the band clause governs, 2029 if the small-cap clause does.

challenges.challenge: QC Q6 unanswered. s4 says the overstated modelled book biases the RI leg low but never sizes it. About Rp322bn (7%) of excess equity lifts RI by about Rp3 a share, or about Rp0.7 on the blend.
challenges.answer: Added a sentence in s4 sizing the excess-equity bias: about three rupiah on the RI leg, under one rupiah on the blend; REDUCE holds.

missing_bull_case.note: Omitted from S10/S11: OJK said MNC Bank core capital 'masih sesuai dengan ketentuan', CAR 24.7% (F16) is far above minimum, OJK called LDR 'biasa naik turun', and the controller's commitment to support capital was noted. BABP free float is 12.76% (below the 15% IDX minimum), so a placement or recapitalisation at bank level is a likely route. Bull ignores historical P/BV 0.35-0.63x.

missing_bear_case.note: Parent equity fell Rp1.19tn in FY2025 (5,775 to 4,586) on Rp256bn profit and a further Rp66bn in 9M2026 (4,520) despite profit; unexplained and not in the bear case. The house's own BABP report is SELL at Rp2.2 against a market price of Rp24, but BCAP's bear case carries no bank write-down, no dilution (share_change 0) and no asset sale despite the narrative. Related-party flows and pledges unquantified.

assumption_realism.note: Three levers: (1) sustainable ROE 5.47% (avg of FY26-28E) vs 6.6% FY2030-35E path; (2) FY2026E ROE 5.6% held on 9M-hit equity: model equity FY26E 4,842 vs 9M actual 4,520, a book path that needs a Q4 gain of about Rp320bn; (3) revenue growth 3-5.5% while the bank must shrink loans. Profit FY26E (256.8) is flat on FY25 (256.1) although 9M consolidated is +18.6%, which is defensible but unreconciled quarter by quarter.

evidence_and_citations.note: Spot checks pass. Weaknesses: insurance revenue mixes definitions (F27 Rp806.3bn = 21.4% FY2025 vs F12 Rp923.8bn = 31.7% for 9M2026, while F26 says 32.0% for FY2025), so 'growing at a double-digit rate' is unverifiable; no LK or annual report read (S2 is navigation only); auditor and related-party sections are 'not sourced'; BABP stake in BCAP not stated anywhere.

valuation_method_fit.note: VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT requires SOTP with honest marks, discount vs own 5y range, upstream dividend coverage and a dated catalyst. The report says SOTP cannot be run because BABP's market value is not in the pack; BABP.JK is covered (price 24, mcap Rp1,067bn, house TP 2.2). Justified P/BV uses g 4% with 0% payout, while RI compounds book at ROE; the two methods are internally inconsistent and the RI -31% divergence is attributed to the wrong cause (terminal treatment of negative RI at 4% growth, pv_tv -1,951). No dated catalyst.

bias_and_tone.note: REDUCE at -22% rests on (a) the 5.47% ROE, (b) a 10% liquidity discount on a stock already at 0.2x book (governance discount counted twice), (c) 30/25 skew; base value alone is Rp18.6-19 (-10%). Prose says the market 'prices correctly' our earnings yet calls the skew asymmetric. Doubling the bear probability is not possible (base 45%); halving the unsourced ROE drift removes the rating. Report claims a mirrored-shock skew justified only by the supervisory case, which is sourced.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Macro deck variables (usd_idr 18350, bi_rate 5.75, cpi 3.28, gdp 5.29) are read consistently with the brief; rf and country premium net of default spread reconcile to COE 12.19%. Sibling consistency with BABP is raised under valuation_method_fit, not here.

conservatism_audit.note: Below last actual/own path without a source: sustainable ROE 5.47% vs 6.6% path and vs last-year-on-current-equity 5.6%; 10% liquidity discount; 0% payout and no bridge/post-BS value (bridge empty); bear/bull shocks mirrored (-/+1pp, -/+2pp) but probabilities 30/25 (sourced narrative); P/E leg dropped; RI terminal growth applied to negative residuals. Each is a challenge; the stack moves the rating.

calibration.note: qc: no blocking flags; FY2025A ROE 4.43% vs model 5.6% (gap +1.17pp, upward because the denominator is the post-fall equity of 4,586, so profit is flat at about 256). weights.changed is justified with S0/S13. Acceptable but note the FY26E/9M equity divergence in C5.

signoff.notes: Round 2: L1 and L2 resolved on substance. s7 and s0 now say 31 Mar 2027 applies only if the band clause governs (31 Mar 2029 under the small-cap clause) and drop 'enforceable'; s4 sizes the equity-path bias (under Rp1 on the blend) and REDUCE holds. C1-C10 answered; check PASS. Comps: BCAP REDUCE -21% is the mildest in a SELL-heavy peer set, WACC 12.2% vs 11.9% argued via beta, no shared-input tilt. Disclosed: REDUCE rests on the 20% RI leg and the 10% liquidity table (justified P/BV alone is near the price); parent equity fall of Rp1,189bn unexplained and flagged as governance/bear item.

bias.note: Base ROE 5.5% flat vs FY2025A 4.4% and LTM 6.4% on current book; FY2026E parent profit 256.8 implies Q4 about 90 consolidated vs 9M run-rate about 61/qtr and strong Q4-25, defensible. FY2027E dip to 5.0% tied to the bank's 105% LDR shrink [S11]. Scenarios mirrored on ROE +/-1pp and growth +/-2pp, 25/50/25. Mild conservatism possible (LTM 6.4% would give about Rp31, Q8) but carried in the bull case. Excess modelled equity (+Rp322bn) biases RI low, sized at under Rp1 on the blend. No unsourced drift.

recomputed.item: Parent equity 30 Sep 2026 and shares (42,618.85m; mcap 895bn at Rp21)

findings.finding: REDUCE depends on the 20% residual-income leg (Rp5 vs justified Rp19) and on the house 10% liquidity discount: on the justified multiple alone the forward value is near Rp21 (about the price). RI divergence is explained (five years of zero payout at ROE below COE, then 27% payout) and sized, but the reader should see the rating hinge.

Parent equity fall of Rp1,189bn in FY2025 is unexplained in any registered source; the report flags it as a governance and bear item and sizes the RI effect. Related-party flows unquantified. Evidence thin, not clean.

Q6 and Q7 are resolved: s4 sizes the RI bias (under Rp1 on the blend) and s7 states both S14 deadlines (31 Mar 2027 band clause, 31 Mar 2029 under Rp5tn) and no longer calls the date enforceable. flags.justification: The long-run payout of 27% from FY2031E is the steady-state identity, not a forecast of generosity: terminal growth of 4% with a 5.5% return on equity requires distributing 1 - 4%/5.5% of earnings for book value to grow at 4%, which is the same identity the justified P/BV leg uses [S0]. The explicit years FY2026E-FY2030E stay at zero because no dividend has ever been paid and OJK is pressing the owner to put capital into the bank [S10, S6].

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'justified_pbv': 0.5, 'pe': 0.3, 'ddm': 0.2}
flags.justification: P/E and DDM are dropped from the industry default blend: the pack's own five-year average P/E rests on crisis-depressed profit and returned a value several times the price, and the group has never paid a dividend, so a DDM is zero by construction [S0, S13]. Justified P/BV and residual income are the methods that price a retained-earnings financial group on its ROE gap to the cost of equity. The residual-income weight is 0.2 rather than 0.4 for a measured reason (QC finding Q1): the engine opens the leg at the 30 September 2026 parent book of Rp4,519.9bn but then rolls equity from the FY2025 close, so the forecast path starts about Rp322bn too high at FY2026E year-end [S0, S6]. Re-running the leg off-engine with the path rebased to the 30 September book (profit following the ROE on the lower book) lifts the residual-income value per share from about Rp4.7 to about Rp11.3 (about Rp13.9 if profit is held at the modelled level), so a 0.4 weight on that leg gives a blend of about Rp15.9, against about Rp16.1 from 0.2 on the engine's own biased leg and 0.8 on justified P/BV (Rp19.0). The 0.2 weight is the weight at which the engine's leg reproduces the rebased 0.4-weight blend. With the leg excluded the target would be about Rp19.7 (TR about -6%, HOLD band); with the unrebased 0.6/0.4 blend it was Rp13.9 (TR -33.7%, SELL). The band therefore moves, and the rating follows the engine at the 0.8/0.2 weights (REDUCE) [S0, S6].
